source_snapshot.procedure: Check that all USB ports can detect a device in BIOS and OS.
source_snapshot.criteria: Make sure the devices can be detected under OS.
source_snapshot.deepseek_package: usbutils + operator to attach the device
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Use lsusb with the device present; the operator handles physical setup and BIOS observation.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that every in-scope physical USB port detects the approved known-good USB device in BIOS and in the installed OS.
original_test_intent.target: The complete engineer-defined USB port/controller matrix and approved test device identity.
original_test_intent.scope: All physical USB ports required by the platform specification, tested port by port in both BIOS and OS; one enumeration snapshot is not all-port coverage.
original_test_intent.operation: An operator moves/attaches the approved device and captures BIOS evidence for each port; the agent collects complete OS USB enumeration/topology and kernel evidence after each placement.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: Twenty minutes attended and 20 minutes machine time; iteration count equals the number of in-scope ports and required device variants.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Each required port enumerates the expected device identity in the required BIOS and OS context without power, controller, driver, mount, boot, or security anomalies.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Port/controller map, per-port device/VID/PID/serial identity, operator placement record, BIOS capture, complete lsusb/topology and kernel evidence, driver state, and coverage matrix.
ambiguities: No port/controller inventory, approved device identity, BIOS method, definition of detected, driver/use requirement, or power/security limits.
source_conflicts: Procedure requires BIOS and OS detection, while Criteria mentions only OS detection.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejected arbitrary devices and one-snapshot coverage, but treated the missing matrix and manual BIOS work as a permanent blocker.

applicable_history.decision: USB attachment and BIOS observation plus automated OS evidence form a hybrid REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION workflow, not BLOCKED.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The all-port USB purpose and hybrid boundary are identifiable. The owner must resolve whether BIOS evidence is mandatory in acceptance and supply the port/device matrix before execution.

available_now: The source names all USB ports and both BIOS/OS contexts; usbutils can collect OS evidence after manual placement.
missing_inputs: Approved device VID/PID/serial, driver and power profile for each port type
BIOS/KVM detection location and whether BIOS evidence is mandatory
Operator sequence and safe removal/restoration procedure
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform owner supplies the port/controller and acceptance matrix; the lab operator supplies and moves the approved device and captures BIOS evidence.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Inventory current USB controllers, hubs, topology, OS devices, drivers, and relevant kernel logs
Confirm no approved device is currently mounted, used as boot media, or security-sensitive
prohibited_until_closed: Do not attach arbitrary, bootable, storage, input, authentication, or over-current devices
Do not use ip link as USB detection evidence
Do not infer all-port coverage from one lsusb output or claim PASS without the coverage matrix
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner confirms the BIOS/OS acceptance scope and supplies a one-to-one port/controller/device matrix; each port receives a planned evidence row and safe operator step.

revision_candidate.test_name: All USB Port Device Detection in BIOS and OS
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify each required physical USB port detects the approved known-good device in BIOS and the installed OS, with complete port-by-port coverage.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified platform revision, BIOS/BMC/OS, USB controller topology, and approved test-device/driver matrix.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every port in the supplied matrix, including front, rear, and internal ports as applicable; map each port to its controller/hub path.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Port/controller map, device identity and power/driver requirements, BIOS/KVM evidence method, definition of detected/usable, operator sequence, usbutils, and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: For each matrix row, the operator connects the approved device and records BIOS detection when required. After OS boot, collect complete lsusb output, USB topology, device/driver details, and kernel enumeration evidence for that placement.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approve the device, confirm no boot/security/storage risk, capture baseline topology/logs, and ensure OOB/alternate-console access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Completed coverage matrix with port/device identity, BIOS capture, OS enumeration/topology/driver evidence, kernel timestamps/errors, and restored final state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The corrected BIOS/OS acceptance statement and platform USB port/device matrix. The engineer decides whether enumeration alone or usable operation is required.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No arbitrary or sensitive USB media, no unexpected mounts, no log clearing, and no coverage claim without per-port evidence.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Approve the matrix/device and every physical attachment sequence; an operator performs placement and BIOS observation.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Physical attachment/movement and BIOS visual evidence are manual; OS enumeration and logs are automatable after each placement.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Safely remove the device, unmount if explicitly permitted and required, restore boot/input/security state, and use OOB access if console or boot is affected.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown port/device identity, unexpected mount or boot behavior, over-current/power error, controller reset, security impact, incomplete coverage, or unresolved BIOS/OS acceptance conflict.

identified_defects: The source procedure and criteria disagree on BIOS acceptance scope.
DeepSeek includes ip link, which is not evidence of USB detection.
V2 over-classifies a hybrid manual-plus-automated workflow as BLOCKED.
reason_for_change: Apply the locked hybrid boundary while preserving the source acceptance-scope conflict and all-port evidence requirement.

new_technical_evidence.supports: All-port and BIOS/OS scope plus OS-only criterion conflict.

removed_ambiguities: Defines all-port coverage as a matrix rather than a single snapshot.
Separates BIOS manual evidence from OS automated evidence and rejects ip link as USB proof.
resolved_blockers: Manual attachment and missing matrix are treated as execution prerequisites instead of permanent non-automability.
remaining_blockers: Execution waits for the corrected BIOS/OS criterion and exact port/device matrix.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's device-safety and coverage warnings but correctly classifies the test as a hybrid workflow, exposes the BIOS-versus-OS source conflict, and defines per-port completion evidence without claiming one lsusb snapshot is sufficient.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The procedure requires every USB port to detect a device in BIOS and OS, but Criteria only names OS.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 rejected arbitrary devices and one-snapshot coverage but called the hybrid case BLOCKED.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Only approved devices may be attached, and completion requires per-port BIOS/OS evidence rather than ip link or one lsusb snapshot.
